title: Finite-field closed-support constructibility
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $k$ a field of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and $A$ a finite field of characteristic $\ell$. Let $g:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use ordinary uncompleted derived categories of module sheaves over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathcal B_A(T)$ for the complexes whose cohomology vanishes outside a finite interval and is constructible [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]: there is a finite constructible locally closed stratification on which each cohomology sheaf is pro-étale locally constant with finite-dimensional $A$-module values. Let $Rg^!$ be the ambient right adjoint to exact closed direct image [lem-exc-proetale-closed-support]. Then $Rg^!\mathcal B_A(T)\subseteq\mathcal B_A(Z)$. No global cohomological-dimension bound on $k$ is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.11, closed-immersion support-triangle proof, specialized to R=A and m=0.

proof.text: Let $j:U=T\setminus g(Z)\hookrightarrow T$ be the complementary open immersion. The spectrum of the field $k$ is Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $T$ Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], $U$ is Noetherian and every open subset of $T$ is quasi-compact. Hence $j$ is quasi-compact: the inverse image of an affine open of $T$ is an open subset of this Noetherian space. By [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] it is locally of finite type, hence finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Applying [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] to $U\to T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ makes $U$ finite type over $k$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.11, proof for a closed immersion, with R=A and m=0; ordinary finite-coefficient specialization.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-intrinsic-finite-derived-pullback], for $h=j$ and $h=g$ the module inverse image is exact, commutes with every cohomology sheaf on the ordinary derived categories, and preserves $\mathcal B_A$ with the same vanishing interval and base-changed finite local models. Both are scheme morphisms and $A$ is a finite field, so all its hypotheses hold.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(5), finite discrete specialization R=A and m=0; Lemma 6.5.8(2) for the open and closed immersions used in Lemma 6.7.11. The exactness and intrinsic stratification argument is isolated from steps 2–3 of lem-sfb-finite-field-closed-support.

proof.text: Fix $K\in\mathcal B_A(T)$. Step 2 gives $j^*K\in\mathcal B_A(U)$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-field-proetale-direct-image] to the finite-type map $j$ of step 1: $Rj_*j^*K\in\mathcal B_A(T)$. The field and coefficient hypotheses are exactly the ones in this item; that theorem does not assume a cohomological-dimension bound on $k$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.11, proof for a closed immersion, with R=A and m=0; ordinary finite-coefficient specialization.

proof.text: By [lem-exc-proetale-support-triangle], in the ambient ordinary derived category there is a distinguished triangle $C\to K\to Rj_*j^*K\to C[1]$, where $C=g_*Rg^!K$. Its exceptional inverse image is the right adjoint of the same closed direct image as in the statement; uniqueness of right adjoints identifies any choices. By [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated], $\mathcal B_A(T)$ is invariant under isomorphisms and shifts and is closed under triangle extensions. Rotate the triangle to $Rj_*j^*K[-1]\to C\to K\to Rj_*j^*K$. Its outer vertices lie in $\mathcal B_A(T)$ by step 3 and the hypothesis on $K$, so $C\in\mathcal B_A(T)$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.11, proof for a closed immersion, with R=A and m=0; ordinary finite-coefficient specialization.

proof.text: Apply $g^*$ to $C$. Step 2 gives $g^*C\in\mathcal B_A(Z)$. The counit $g^*g_*M\to M$ is an isomorphism for every module sheaf $M$ by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful], and $g_*$ is exact by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact], since its complementary open immersion is quasi-compact by step 1. Both functors therefore descend termwise to ordinary derived categories; applying the sheaf counit degree by degree to any representative of $Rg^!K$ yields $g^*g_*Rg^!K\cong Rg^!K$. Consequently $Rg^!K\in\mathcal B_A(Z)$ by the isomorphism invariance in [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated]. For $Z=∅$ the value is zero; for $Z=T$ the counit gives $K$. No field cohomological-dimension bound is used.
